problem.value: Computer vision lacks a foundation model for image segmentation that can generalize via prompt engineering.

evidence.quote: In this work, our goal is to build a foundation model for image segmentation.

problem.value: Abundant training data does not exist for many computer vision problems beyond vision and language encoders.

evidence.quote: While much progress has been made on vision and language encoders, computer vision includes a wide range of problems beyond this scope, and for many of these, abundant training data does not exist.

contributions.value: Proposed the promptable segmentation task as a pre-training objective and zero-shot transfer mechanism.

evidence.quote: We use the promptable segmentation task as both a pre-training objective and to solve general downstream segmentation tasks via prompt engineering.

contributions.value: Developed the Segment Anything Model (SAM) with a lightweight mask decoder for real-time promptable segmentation.

evidence.quote: We refer to this model as the Segment Anything Model, or SAM (see Fig. 1b).

contributions.value: Built a data engine using model-in-the-loop annotation to collect a massive dataset.

evidence.quote: Our solution is to build a "data engine", i.e., we co-develop our model with model-in-the-loop dataset annotation (see Fig. 1c).

contributions.value: Created the SA-1B dataset containing over 1 billion masks from 11 million images.

evidence.quote: Our final dataset, SA-1B, includes more than 1B masks from 11M licensed and privacy-preserving images (see Fig. 2).
Inspired by this line of work, we propose the promptable segmentation task, where the goal is to return a valid segmentation mask given any segmentation prompt (see Fig. 1a).

method_summary.value: SAM consists of three core components: an image encoder, a flexible prompt encoder, and a fast mask decoder.

evidence.quote: SAM has three components, illustrated in Fig. 4: an image encoder, a flexible prompt encoder, and a fast mask decoder.

method_summary.value: The image encoder uses a Vision Transformer pre-trained with MAE, minimally adapted for high-resolution inputs, running once per image.

evidence.quote: Motivated by scalability and powerful pretraining methods, we use an MAE [47] pre-trained Vision Transformer (ViT) [33] minimally adapted to process high resolution inputs [62].

method_summary.value: The prompt encoder handles sparse prompts like points, boxes, and text using positional and learned embeddings, and dense prompts like masks using convolutions.

evidence.quote: We consider two sets of prompts: sparse (points, boxes, text) and dense (masks).

method_summary.value: The mask decoder combines image and prompt embeddings via a modified Transformer decoder block and outputs dynamic mask predictions.

evidence.quote: This design, inspired by [14,20], employs a modification of a Transformer decoder block [103] followed by a dynamic mask prediction head.

method_summary.value: To resolve ambiguity, the model predicts multiple masks simultaneously using separate output tokens and backpropagates only the minimum loss.

evidence.quote: To address this, we modify the model to predict multiple output masks for a single prompt (see Fig. 3).

method_summary.value: The model is supervised using a linear combination of focal loss and dice loss, trained by simulating interactive prompt sequences across multiple iterations.

evidence.quote: We supervise mask prediction with the linear combination of focal loss [65] and dice loss [73] used in [14].

claims.value: SAM produces high-quality masks from a single foreground point across 23 diverse segmentation datasets.

evidence.quote: First, using a diverse new suite of 23 segmentation datasets, we find that SAM produces high-quality masks from a single foreground point, often only slightly below that of the manually annotated ground truth.

claims.value: SA-1B has 400 times more masks than any existing segmentation dataset.

evidence.quote: SA-1B, collected fully automatically using the final stage of our data engine, has 400× more masks than any existing segmentation dataset [66,44,117,60], and as we verify extensively, the masks are of high quality and diversity.

claims.value: The prompt encoder and mask decoder can predict a mask from a prompt in about 50 milliseconds.

evidence.quote: Given an image embedding, the prompt encoder and mask decoder predict a mask from a prompt in ∼50ms in a web browser.

claims.value: SAM demonstrates consistently strong quantitative and qualitative results on various downstream tasks under a zero-shot transfer protocol.

evidence.quote: Second, we find consistently strong quantitative and qualitative results on a variety of downstream tasks under a zero-shot transfer protocol using prompt engineering, including edge detection, object proposal generation, instance segmentation, and a preliminary exploration of text-to-mask prediction.
